chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
When it is the morning of the Day of Fitr, a caller proclaims: 'Go forth to your awards!'
ai.seo_question: What happens on the morning of Eid al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the metaphor of a public crier announcing 'go to your awards' to emphasize the tangible spiritual rewards awaiting those who complete Ramadan's fasts. This imagery reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of Eid as a celebration of divine grace and the fulfillment of religious duty, linking the physical act of fasting to the metaphysical receipt of God's bounty. It underscores the joyous nature of the occasion as a moment of divine recognition for the believer's perseverance.
